Now, "push the silver colored part to the right." The silver part is the handle. The handle is above the base. If I push the top of the handle to the right, the handle will tilt/fall to the right.

So the handle, which is attached at the base (the top of the teal part), will rotate around that pivot point. Pushing it to the right means the top of the handle moves to the right. When it falls completely, it will be lying on the ground to the right of the base.

Wait, but I need to consider the perspective. The camera is looking at the kettlebell. The handle points up. "Right" in the image corresponds to the right side.

Let me think about the pivot. The handle is attached to the top of the base. The base is on the floor. When the kettlebell falls, the handle tip will move toward the floor on the right side. So the handle will end up lying on the ground pointing to the right of the base.

So the handle will be to the right of the base. That's option D.

But wait, let me double check the orientation. The handle is vertical. The base is below it. If I push the top of the handle to the right (in the image's right direction), the handle rotates clockwise (from the viewer's perspective). When it falls flat, the handle points to the right. So the handle is to the right of the base. Yes, D.

Let me consider the other options. "In front of the base" would mean the handle falls toward the camera. "Behind" would mean away from camera. "Left" would mean to the left.

Since we push to the right, the handle falls to the right. So D.

Let me double check by thinking about the push direction more carefully. The gripper pushes the silver part. The silver part is the handle, which is at the top. Pushing it right makes it tilt right. So it falls to the right. The handle will be to the right of the base.

Thus answer D.

The question is straightforward. The answer is D.
